question: Does the already-available public FrontBlocked sensor suffice to predict whether action=2 physically changes position in the original FIT transitions, compared with matched empirical conventional controls? No inference about goal completion.

models.unconditional: training majority probability for movement irrespective of FrontBlocked, per curriculum and family
models.direction_only: training majority probability by public direction, with unobserved states fallback to unconditional
models.learned_public_blocked: Laplace-smoothed empirical P(move|FrontBlocked) trained only on FIT reconstruction subset per curriculum and family; 2 class counts per stratum
models.published_sensor_rule: untrained direct prediction move = not FrontBlocked; explicitly information-advantaged public sensor reference, not native learner
models.ablated_shuffled_sensor: deterministically shuffle public FrontBlocked training labels within each family and curriculum (Random(20261024)), fit identical learned count to break historical association

evaluation.predict: physical position changed after action2, not goal success; both original processes are corroboration not independent hosts
evaluation.mandatory_original_counterfactual: never infer unexecuted actions; only rows where original action==2 are eligible
evaluation.accuracy_first: count TP/TN/FP/FN and per-stratum counts; include balanced accuracy because class imbalance
evaluation.frozen_criterion: if learned sensor stratification is perfect on each family and curriculum and beats unconditional in random curriculum by >=0.05 balanced accuracy, label K4Y_PUBLIC_FORWARD_CONSEQUENCE_IDENTIFIABLE_IN_RECORDED_FIT; otherwise K4Y_NOT_IDENTIFIED
evaluation.condition_for_novelty: Even if pass, strong learned-count conventional control solves the one-step signal; NO novelty, no novel native transfer, no unconsumed DEV evaluation

record_full_host_resource: whole process wall and CPU seconds, Python ru_maxrss only; no FLOP/energy claim
